title: The Overdue filter must remain special-cased against isOverdue, never regress to a literal normalizedStatus='overdue' match
description: TK-007 (Sprint 3B, fixed): before the fix, `normalizedStatus === 'overdue'` was compared literally against task.normalizedStatus, which is never actually 'overdue' — the Overdue summary card/filter matched zero tasks. The fix in tasks.service.js special-cases this exact filter value: `if (normalizedStatus === 'overdue') { filtered = filtered.filter(t => t.isOverdue && t.normalizedStatus !== 'done'); }`.
preconditions: At least one task with dueDate in the past and normalizedStatus='pending', plus non-overdue tasks
expectedResult: Only tasks where isOverdue=true AND normalizedStatus != 'done' are returned. Must not regress to returning zero results (the pre-fix behavior).

title: WorkflowEntry evidence/policy tasks must remain org-scoped via the Evidence/Policy post-filter
description: TK-009 (Sprint 3B, fixed): WorkflowEntry queries originally had no organizationId filter at all, so evidence/policy review tasks assigned to a user leaked across organizations whenever a WorkflowEntry referenced an entity outside the caller's org. The fix added fetchWorkflowEntries()'s post-fetch filter against the Evidence/Policy collection scoped by organizationId.
preconditions: A WorkflowEntry assigns the test user to review an evidence/policy item belonging to a DIFFERENT organization than the one the user is querying as
steps: Call GET /api/tasks as the test user scoped to their own organization
expectedResult: The cross-org WorkflowEntry task never appears. Must not regress to WORKFLOW_ENTITY_MODEL post-filter being removed or bypassed.

title: risk-management-service must declare userOid before use and compare riskOwner.userId/treatment.leadOwner.userId as ObjectId, not as a raw string
description: TK-010 (fixed as ObjectId comparison) was re-opened as TK-019 (Run 3) after the fix introduced a ReferenceError: `userOid` was referenced in the ownerRisks/leadOwnerRisks queries but never declared before use, crashing every call to this endpoint. Current source confirms `let userOid: ObjectId; try { userOid = new ObjectId(userId); }` is declared before both queries that reference it (riskOwner.userId, treatment.leadOwner.userId).
preconditions: A Risk document has riskOwner.userId stored as a genuine ObjectId (not a string) equal to the test user's id
steps: Call GET http://risk-management-service/internal/tasks?userId=<test user>&organizationId=<org> with a valid X-Internal-Token
expectedResult: 200 with the risk correctly included in the tasks array — no ReferenceError / 500, and the ObjectId-typed field match succeeds (would silently miss the risk entirely if compared as a string against an ObjectId field).

title: Done/closed items must remain excluded from AuditScopeItem and ContinuousImprovement task queries
description: TK-013 (fixed): AuditScopeItem's Mongo query must keep `assessmentStatus: { $nin: ['closed', 'not_applicable'] }` (applied on both the direct-assignee and WorkflowEntry-fallback branches), and the ContinuousImprovement flatMap must keep filtering out `!['completed','cancelled'].includes(init.status)` — otherwise closed/completed items reappear as open tasks, inflating pending/in_progress counts and cluttering the Owner tab with already-finished work.
preconditions: An AuditScopeItem assigned to the user has assessmentStatus='closed'
A ContinuousImprovement initiative assigned to the user has status='completed'
expectedResult: Neither the closed scope item nor the completed initiative appears in data.tasks.

title: A null assignedTo on a ManagementReview action item or ContinuousImprovement initiative must not crash GET /api/tasks
description: TK-014 and TK-018 (both fixed): the flatMap filters `item.assignedTo && item.assignedTo.toString() === userIdStr` (ManagementReview) and `init.assignedTo && init.assignedTo.toString() === userIdStr` (ContinuousImprovement) must keep the leading null-guard — removing it re-introduces a TypeError on `.toString()` of null/undefined for any unassigned item, which is NOT caught by the outer try/catch (that only wraps the earlier Promise.all of the 9 internal source queries, not this later flatMap step).
preconditions: A ManagementReview document has one actionItem with assignedTo=null mixed with others assigned to the test user
A ContinuousImprovement document has an analogous unassigned initiative
steps: Call GET /api/tasks as the test user who owns the OTHER items in those same parent documents
expectedResult: 200 response, no 500/crash. The null-assignedTo items are silently skipped; the user's own properly-assigned items still appear.

title: A single internal-source model throw must not crash the entire GET /api/tasks response
description: TK-017 (fixed): the outer try/catch around the Promise.all of the 9 internal-source sub-queries falls back to `_internalRaw = [[], [], [], [], [], [], [], [], []]` on any unexpected throw (e.g. ObjectId construction failure surfacing unexpectedly, or a model registration edge case not already guarded by the inner per-query try/catch). Must not regress to an unguarded Promise.all whose rejection propagates as an unhandled 500.
preconditions: Simulate one internal sub-query throwing synchronously outside its own inner try/catch (e.g. via a mocked Mongoose model)
steps: Call GET /api/tasks while the fault-injected model is active
expectedResult: 200 response with the 8 remaining internal arrays emptied (fallback) rather than the whole endpoint returning 500 — microservice fan-out and any working internal sources still get a chance to run/merge (or return an empty-but-valid result if the fallback path was hit before them).

title: Summary card counts still shift when any filter is applied — known open gap, not yet fixed
description: TK-021 (open): tasks.service.js builds `summary` and `byModule` from `filtered` (the array AFTER sourceModule/normalizedStatus/priority/projectScope/dueBefore/search/assignmentType are all applied), not from the full pre-filter task set. This means the 4 TaskSummaryBar stat cards (Pending/In Progress/Overdue/Done) do not represent 'all my tasks' once any other filter (e.g. sourceModule=risk) is active — they silently narrow to match that filter too, which can read as the cards themselves being broken rather than reflecting the current filter combination.
preconditions: User has open tasks across at least 2 different sourceModule values with a mix of pending/in_progress/overdue statuses
steps: Navigate to /tasks with no filters, note the 4 summary card numbers
Apply sourceModule=risk via the Module dropdown
expectedResult: Current behavior: the summary card numbers change to reflect ONLY risk-module tasks after the module filter is applied — they do not stay fixed at the org-wide 'all my tasks' totals. This is a known, still-open gap (TK-021); this case exists to detect the day it silently changes (fixed OR made worse) rather than to assert it as correct.

title: DueDateCell and AssignedCell still render a blank cell (not '—') when date parsing throws — known open gap, not yet fixed
description: TK-023 (open): both cells guard the missing-value case (`if (!task.dueDate) return <Text>—</Text>`) but the try/catch around date-fns format()/formatDistanceToNow() returns `null` on a parse error rather than falling back to the same '—' placeholder used for the missing-value case. A malformed date string (as opposed to an absent one) therefore renders as a visually blank cell instead of a dash, which is easy to misread as a rendering failure.
preconditions: A task's dueDate (or assignedAt) contains a value that is present but fails Date parsing, e.g. an empty string or a non-ISO garbage value from a misbehaving upstream source
steps: Render the tasks table with a row whose dueDate is a non-empty but unparseable string
expectedResult: Current behavior: the Due Date cell for that row is completely blank (catch block returns null), inconsistent with the '—' shown for a genuinely absent dueDate. This case exists to detect whether a future fix aligns the two fallback paths, or whether the gap persists/worsens.
